recent_articles.title: Meenakshi Natarajan Row And Congress' Article 324 Demand. What It Is
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Congress** leader Meenakshi Natarajan's Rajya Sabha nomination was rejected for nondisclosure of a pending court case. The party is urging the **Election Commission (EC)** to use its powers under Article 324 to overturn the Returning Officer's decision, arguing that the alleged omission does not warrant disqualification.  The EC has the power to oversee elections and ensure free and fair processes, but experts question whether this provision can override specific legal provisions or be used as a substitute for existing remedies like Election Petitions. The EC is currently examining the Congress' representation and seeking the Returning Officer's report before making a decision.

recent_articles.title: Court directs to frame charges against Sukesh Chandrasekhar, Jacqueline Fernandes, others in PMLA case | Today News
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sukesh Chandrasekhar**, **Leena Maria Paul**, and several others were ordered by a court in Patiala House Courts to face charges in a money laundering case linked to the alleged ₹200-crore extortion of Aditi Singh.  The court also directed charges be framed against them in a separate case under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act related to the same alleged extortion. **Jacqueline Fernandez** was not named as an accused in the extortion case, and her bail application is currently pending before the High Court. The Delhi Police filed a case on the complaint of Aditi Singh, which led to the Enforcement Directorate lodging a money laundering case.

recent_articles.title: Jacqueline Fernandez, Conman Sukesh Face Charges In Money Laundering Case
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A **Delhi** court has ordered charges to be framed against **Jacqueline Fernandez**, **Sukesh Chandrashekar**, and 15 others in a Rs 200-crore money laundering case. The prosecution alleges that the accused, including **Chandrashekhar**, who was arrested for bribery, used spoofed calls and fabricated identities to extort money from individuals. They are accused of concealing proceeds of crime through various channels, using them to purchase property, luxury vehicles, and gifts.  The Enforcement Directorate (ED) has collected digital evidence, including mobile phone records and financial transactions, linking the accused to the alleged money laundering scheme.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal election: Why politicians are campaigning with fish in hand
recent_articles.rephrased_article: In the upcoming West Bengal assembly elections, **Indian politicians** are using fish as a political symbol to appeal to voters.  The BJP is attempting to counter accusations of interfering with Bengali culture by highlighting their own connection to fish consumption and local production. The ruling Trinamool Congress accuses the BJP of trying to restrict fish consumption, while the BJP claims that the Trinamool Congress has failed to provide Bengal with enough fish. Both parties are using fish as a way to appeal to voters' cultural identities and anxieties about food security.

recent_articles.title: Ceasefire calm sparks bargain hunting in beaten-down stocks - The Economic Times
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Helios India's** Dinshaw Irani cautioned against investing in beaten-down stocks hoping for a rebound, as the recent market sell-off was broad-based.  While sectors like oil and gas saw gains following a two-week ceasefire in the **West Asia** conflict, analysts like **Angel One's** Aamar Deo Singh noted that bargain-hunting is concentrated in quality large-caps within banks, pharmaceuticals, and FMCG due to their resilience during the conflict. However, sustained high oil prices may pose headwinds for these sectors unless they fall below $80 a barrel.

recent_articles.title: 'They asked for 7, I gave them 10': Donald Trump reveals Iran's 'big present' to US as Hormuz deadline delayed - The Times of India
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Donald Trump** granted **Iran** a 10-day extension on the pause of planned military strikes against its energy infrastructure, citing ongoing diplomatic efforts. The move followed a request from **Iranian** officials who wanted more time to engage in negotiations.  The US President also acknowledged that Iran allowed eight oil tankers through the Strait of Hormuz as part of this agreement. Trump stated that talks are progressing well and he is hopeful for a complete resolution of hostilities in the Middle East.
